College Packing Checklist

Packing for college is a balancing act — bring enough to feel at home in a small dorm room, but not so much it won't fit. This college packing checklist covers the essentials students actually use, from twin XL bedding to a power strip and a basic first-aid kit, and flags what to check with your roommate before doubling up. See more study and school checklists.

verified Curated by the Gisti team · Updated July 2026

College Packing Checklist · 20 items

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Twin XL sheets, a mattress topper, pillows, and a comforter

    Most dorm beds are twin XL, not standard twin — check first.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Mattress protector and an extra set of sheets
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Bath towels, a hand towel, and a quick-dry shower towel
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Shower caddy and flip-flops for shared bathrooms

    Flip-flops are non-negotiable in communal showers.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Toiletries, a toothbrush holder, and a refillable water bottle
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Laptop, charger, and a padded sleeve or bag
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Power strip with surge protection and a couple of extension cords

    Dorm outlets are always too few and too far away.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Phone charger, headphones, and any adapters you need
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Desk lamp and a small clip-on reading light
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Notebooks, pens, highlighters, sticky notes, and a planner
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Backpack for class and a reusable water bottle
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Under-bed storage bins and a few drawer organizers

    Vertical and under-bed space is where dorms hide extra room.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Laundry hamper, detergent pods, and a roll of quarters or a laundry card
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Basic first-aid kit and any daily medications

    Include pain relievers, bandages, and a thermometer.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Mini fridge or microwave — coordinate so you and your roommate don't both bring one

    Message your roommate before move-in day.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    A few mugs, plates, utensils, and a reusable food container
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Command hooks, poster strips, and a small toolkit

    Adhesive hooks save your deposit — no nails in dorm walls.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Fan, plus a warm blanket or throw for cold nights
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Important documents: ID, insurance card, and a copy of your housing and class schedule
  • check_box_outline_blank
    A little decor — photos, string lights, or a rug to make the room yours

Frequently asked questions

What size sheets do I need for a dorm bed? expand_more

Most college dorm beds use a twin XL mattress, which is longer than a standard twin. Buy twin XL sheets and a twin XL mattress topper, and confirm the size with your housing office before you shop, since a small number of dorms use standard twin or full beds.

What should I not bring to college? expand_more

Skip candles, halogen lamps, and most hot plates or space heaters — they usually break fire-safety rules. Don't double up on big items like a fridge, microwave, or TV; coordinate with your roommate first. And leave anything you rarely use at home, since dorm rooms are small and storage is tight.

What is the most forgotten item when packing for college? expand_more

The commonly forgotten ones are a surge-protected power strip, shower flip-flops, a basic first-aid kit, and spare phone and laptop chargers. A small toolkit, command hooks, and a mattress topper are also easy to overlook but make dorm life much more comfortable.
